presentation_summary: Woman referred with a six-year history of polymyositis that began at age 43, now with severe proximal upper and lower limb weakness, difficulty standing, and severe dysphagia.
At referral she was unable to walk or stand unaided, had dysphagia with further weight loss from 44 kg to 40 kg, CK 397 IU/L, muscle weakness score 55/88, and myositis activity scale 49/75.
Prior biopsy-confirmed polymyositis, repeat biopsy, EMG, myositis-specific antibodies, prior diagnosis, and response to subcutaneous immunoglobulin are confirmatory/non-ranking.

risk_context.source_text_value: long treatment history including corticosteroids, methotrexate or azathioprine, rituximab, cyclosporine, tacrolimus, plasma exchange, and IVIg

observations.source_text_value: severe proximal muscular weakness in upper and lower limbs
proximal weakness with neck flexor involvement
unable to walk or stand unaided
weight decreased from 44 kg to 40 kg before SCIg

confirmatory_findings.finding: Prior diagnosis of polymyositis was biopsy-confirmed
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: diagnosis of polymyositis was confirmed by a muscle biopsy

confirmatory_findings.finding: Muscle biopsy showed CD8 endomysial inflammatory infiltrates invading nonnecrotic fibers and MHC-I expression
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: endomysial inflammatory infiltrates surrounding and invading nonnecrotic muscle fibers

confirmatory_findings.finding: Biopsy lacked rimmed vacuoles, ragged red fibers, and COX-negative fibers suggesting IBM
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: rimmed vacuoles, ragged red fibers, and cytochrome oxidase-negative fibers were not observed

confirmatory_findings.finding: EMG showed active myopathic motor unit changes
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: fibrillation potentials, positive sharp waves, and short duration small amplitude polyphasic MUAPs

confirmatory_findings.finding: Second biopsy confirmed active polymyositis before SCIg
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: a second muscle biopsy confirmed the active polymyositis

actual_treatment.name: subcutaneous_immunoglobulin
actual_treatment.source_text_value: SCIg was initiated after difficult venous access and benefit from immunoglobulins

outcome.source_text_value: CK normalized, patient walked unaided, and dysphagia resolved after SCIg and rehabilitation

quality_warnings: Known prior polymyositis diagnosis, biopsies, EMG, antibody status, and treatment response are confirmatory/non-ranking.
The rankable presentation keeps the refractory functional phenotype: severe proximal weakness, dysphagia, weight loss, and CK elevation.
